jobs.title: Jr. Software Engineer
jobs.description:
NBCUniversal is one of the world's leading media and entertainment companies. We create world-class content, which we distribute across our portfolio of film, television, and streaming, and bring to life through our global theme park destinations, consumer products, and experiences. We own and operate leading entertainment and news brands, including NBC, NBC News, NBC Sports, Telemundo, NBC Local Stations, Bravo, and Peacock, our premium ad-supported streaming service. We produce and distribute premier filmed entertainment and programming through our powerhouse film and television studios, including Universal Pictures, DreamWorks Animation, and Focus Features, and the four global television studios under the Universal Studio Group banner, and operate industry-leading theme parks and experiences around the world through Universal Destinations & Experiences, including Universal Orlando Resort, home to Universal Epic Universe, and Universal Studios Hollywood. NBCUniversal is a subsidiary of Comcast Corporation. Visit www.nbcuniversal.com for more information.

Our impact is rooted in improving the communities where our employees, customers, and audiences live and work. We have a rich tradition of giving back and ensuring our employees have the opportunity to serve their communities. We champion an inclusive culture and strive to attract and develop a talented workforce to create and deliver a wide range of content reflecting our world.

Job Description

NBCUniversal’s Intellectual Property Analytics, Operations, and Technology (IPAOT) team supports NBCUniversal’s content globally with four key areas: (1) developing more secure and scalable frameworks for Internet-based video distribution, (2) improving security technologies and processes in content production and distribution, (3) addressing voluminous copyright infringements on websites, apps and protocols, and (4) analyzing data to measure and understand the drivers of unlicensed video consumption on the Internet.

The IPAOT team at NBCUniversal is looking for a passionate and curious Jr. Software Engineer to help design, build, and maintain applications supporting content protection, investigations, analytics, and security. This role will have a particular focus on expanding the use of artificial intelligence and large language models (LLMs) across the team's application portfolio, identifying opportunities to enhance existing workflows and develop new AI-powered capabilities.

Reporting to the Manager, Product and Emerging Technology
, the Jr. Software Engineer is a fast-paced role with opportunities to work across traditional software engineering, generative AI, emerging technologies, and content protection.

Responsibilities

Develop and enhance AI-powered features across the team’s applications using large language models and other AI technologies.
Build LLM-powered applications and agentic workflows using model APIs, retrieval technologies, and supporting frameworks.
Integrate AI models and services into existing applications based on defined requirements
Develop and refine prompts, system instructions, and model interactions to improve application performance and reliability
Build integrations with internal systems, tools, and data sources using APIs, MCPs, and other technologies
Support monitoring, testing, and evaluation of AI-powered features.
Collaborate with product and business stakeholders to translate requirements into working features and improvements.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related STEM field, or equivalent professional experience.
1 + years of professional software development experience, including experience developing and delivering software to production.
Programming experience with Python and JavaScript/TypeScript.
Experience developing modern web applications and backend APIs using frameworks such as Next.js, FastAPI, or comparable technologies.
Hands-on experience developing applications or features using large language models through APIs.
Experience integrating APIs, backend services, and third-party systems.
Experience working with relational databases and SQL.
Familiarity with modern software development practices including source control, testing, debugging, and code review.
Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related STEM field.
Experience building LLM-powered workflows using LangChain or similar frameworks
Familiarity with multiple LLM providers and model platforms such as OpenRouter.
Experience with LLM evaluation and observability tools such as LangSmith, Langfuse, or similar technologies.
Experience with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, vector databases, or semantic search.
Experience developing cloud-based applications, preferably using AWS.
Familiarity with video technologies, streaming media, content protection, cybersecurity, or digital rights management.
Interest in emerging AI technologies and their practical application in software development.

Additional Requirements:

Hybrid:
This position currently has a hybrid schedule, which requires contributing from the office a minimum of four
days per week. The Company reserves the right to change in-office requirements at any time.

This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: $62,000 - $80,000.

Additional Information

As part of our selection process, external candidates may be required to attend an in-person interview with an NBCUniversal employee at one of our locations prior to a hiring decision. NBCUniversal's policy is to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, gender identity or expression, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy, veteran status, membership in the uniformed services, genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
We're looking for an experienced, forward-thinking engineer to strengthen our Platform Engineering capabilities across AWS and Windows environments, with a focus on authentication, certificate services and encryption. In this role, you'll design and automate the identity and cryptographic services that our Infrastructure and Application stack depends on, from certificate lifecycle automation at enterprise scale through to directory, authentication and key management. You'll work closely with diverse technology teams to streamline delivery, embed security best practices, and champion infrastructure-as-code. If you're passionate about automation, cloud-native patterns, and making critical services resilient, we want to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities

Design, implement, and manage scalable and resilient infrastructure on AWS.
Design and automate the certificate lifecycle at enterprise scale, covering issuance, validation, renewal, revocation and deployment to target workloads.
Design, maintain and improve the resilience of Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), including certificate authority operation, certificate inventory and expiry alerting.
Build event-driven automation in AWS using services such as EventBridge, Lambda, Secrets Manager, Systems Manager and S3.
Deploy and bind certificates to AWS managed services and to Windows and Linux web and application servers.
Design and maintain multi-account AWS patterns, including cross-account IAM, resource policies and KMS key policies.
Administer, secure and improve the resilience of Active Directory and DNS.
Support and advance Windows authentication, including Kerberos, delegation and service account models.
Implement encryption for data at rest and in transit, and manage keys, rotation and key access policy.
Develop and maintain infrastructure-as-code (IaC) using both Terraform (OpenTofu) and AWS CloudFormation/CDK.
Develop and maintain Configuration Management for Windows servers using Chef, AWS SSM or Ansible.
Design, build, and optimize CI/CD pipelines using GitLab CI/CD.
Implement and enforce security best practices across the infrastructure and deployment processes.
Collaborate closely with development teams to understand their needs and provide Platform Engineering expertise.
Troubleshoot and resolve infrastructure and application deployment issues.
Implement and manage monitoring, logging and alerting to ensure system visibility and proactive issue detection.
Clearly and concisely contribute to the development and documentation of Platform standards and best practices.
Provide mentorship and guidance to junior team members.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
7+ years of experience in a Platform Engineering, DevOps or Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) role.
Extensive hands-on experience with Amazon Web Services (AWS), including ACM, KMS, Secrets Manager, Systems Manager, IAM, EventBridge, Lambda and S3.
Experience designing and operating multi-account AWS environments, including cross-account IAM, resource policies and KMS key policies.
Strong Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and certificate lifecycle experience, including certificate authority operation, certificate formats, chain assembly, renewal automation and revocation.
Experience deploying and binding certificates on Windows (IIS) and Linux (Nginx, Apache, Tomcat) servers.
Strong Active Directory experience, including replication, FSMO roles, trust relationships and AD-integrated DNS.
Strong understanding of Windows authentication protocols, specifically Kerberos and NTLM, including service principal names, delegation, supported encryption types and service account models.
Practical experience with encryption at rest and in transit, and with key management services.
Solid understanding of Windows Server administration and integration with cloud environments.
Proven experience with infrastructure-as-code (IaC) tools, specifically Terraform (OpenTofu) and AWS CDK.
Strong experience designing and implementing CI/CD pipelines using GitLab CI/CD.
Deep understanding of security best practices and their implementation in cloud infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines.
Solid understanding of networking principles (TCP/IP, DNS, load balancing, firewalls) in cloud environments.
Experience with monitoring and logging tools (e.g., NewRelic, CloudWatch, Cloud Logging, Prometheus).
Strong scripting skills, with PowerShell at an advanced level, plus Python or Bash.
Experience with configuration management tools, such as Chef, AWS SSM, or Ansible.
Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
Strong communication and collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

AWS Certified Security – Specialty, or other relevant AWS certifications, are a plus.
Experience with certificate automation protocols and tooling (e.g., ACME, cert-manager or equivalent).
Experience operating a private certificate authority.
Experience with multi-tenant platforms and namespace isolation.
Experience hardening Active Directory against credential attacks.
Experience with Microsoft Entra ID and hybrid identity integration is a plus.
Experience with disaster recovery design for critical services, including defined RTO and RPO targets.
Strong background with AWS EC2 features and Services (Autoscaling and WarmPools)
Understanding of Windows server Build process using tools like Chocolatey for packages and Packer for AMI/Image generation.
Solid experience with the Windows server operating system and server tools such as IIS.
Experience with containerization & orchestration technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) is a plus.

Hira is an automation platform that streamlines the job application process using dedicated personal agents that operate continuously to identify strong career opportunities. jobs.title: Software Developer
jobs.description:
Alive & Kickin' Pizza Crust is seeking a full-time Software Developer. This is our first dedicated development role, created to take ownership of the internal development work our IT department has been absorbing. You will take technical problems from the IT department and our business analysts and turn them into working solutions — automation scripts, internal web applications, ERP integrations, and Power Automate and AI-assisted workflows that remove manual effort from the business.

Reporting to the IT Director, you will be the sole software developer in the organization and will work closely with our business analysts, data analyst, and the end users who depend on these systems every day. This is a broad role with real autonomy where you will see problems end to end, from requirements through deployment and support.

Key Responsibilities:

Problem Intake & Solution Development:

• Take in technical problems and requests from the IT department and business analysts, scope them, and deliver practical solutions.
• Evaluate whether a problem is best solved with a script, a web tool, an ERP customization, a low-code workflow, or a process change — and make that recommendation.
• Own the full lifecycle: requirements, development, testing, deployment, documentation, and ongoing support.
• Identify automation opportunities proactively by observing how teams work, rather than waiting for requests.

Automation & Scripting:

• Design, build, and maintain Python and PowerShell automation that eliminates manual, repetitive work across the business.
• Build and maintain workflows in Microsoft Power Automate, including approvals, notifications, and system-to-system handoffs.
• Apply AI and large language model (LLM) capabilities where they add practical value — for example, using AI APIs and Microsoft Copilot services in Python-based scripts and workflows to classify, summarize, or extract information from unstructured data.
• Schedule, monitor, and support automation running on Windows Server and in Azure.

Internal Web Development:

• Build and maintain internal websites, dashboards, and tools used by staff across the company.
• Deploy and maintain those applications on internal web servers (IIS) and in Azure.
• Apply secure development practices — authentication, authorization, input validation, and least-privilege access.

ERP & Business Systems Integration:

• Integrate custom solutions with our ERP platform, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, and with our MES and other line-of-business systems.
• Build and consume REST APIs to move data reliably between systems.
• Develop, test, and deploy Business Central extensions as needed, and validate existing customizations against Business Central release waves and updates.
• Support our data analyst with data ingestion, pipelines, and transformation work in Microsoft Fabric, and help troubleshoot data quality and pipeline reliability issues.
General IT Support & Practices
• Learn our ERP and MES platforms and become a trusted technical resource for both.
• Assist the IT team with general support tasks as needed, such as endpoint issues, Microsoft 365 administration, and user support during busy periods or coverage gaps.
• Follow change management and version control practices and keep technical documentation current.

Requirements:

• Associate or bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, MIS, or a related field — or equivalent demonstrated experience.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Prolaio believes that continuous learning and collaboration can make a significant difference in how heart care is administered. We are creating smarter ways to address heart disease and heart risks by uniting patients, care teams, and researchers on a secure, technology-enabled platform that drives clinical innovation and offers a path towards better patient outcomes.
This is precision cardiology, and we know it’s within reach.

What Will You Do?

The Overview

The Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) will ensure that Prolaio’s cardiovascular data platform reliably captures, transports, and delivers continuous biosensor data from participants to the clinical researchers and trial sponsors who depend on it. In this role, you will build and operate the monitoring, service level objectives, incident response, and automation needed to keep critical data flows healthy, identify failures before they impact studies, and ensure that device downtime never goes unnoticed simply because a shipment record says a device was delivered.

This role is ideal for a self-starter who thrives at the intersection of software reliability, connected devices, and clinical data. You will investigate incidents across the full participant-to-platform stack, combining service telemetry with device data and participant reports to determine whether an issue originated with the hardware, phone, firmware, mobile application, connectivity, or the platform itself. You will turn those investigations into durable improvements, automating manual checks, strengthening observability, reducing operational toil, and building the reliability practices that keep Prolaio’s clinical data complete and trustworthy at scale.

The Specifics

Build monitoring that treats missing data as a failure rather than a quiet day — freshness, volume and quality checks that verify delivery from outside the system instead of trusting a job's exit code.
Define and maintain SLIs, SLOs and error budgets for customer-facing data services, and report attainment honestly, including when the news is bad.
Join the on-call rotation, run incident response, and write blameless postmortems that produce owned follow-up actions.
Investigate device failures end to end: correlate discharge curves, Bluetooth disconnects and wear detection against the participant's complaint, and establish or exonerate each candidate cause on evidence.
Treat the fleet as a population — failure rates per device-month, clustering by build lot, firmware version or site — rather than as a queue of individual tickets.
Close the loop. When an analysis cannot reach a verdict, name the missing metric or threshold and route it back into the diagnostics pipeline so the next case is answerable from telemetry alone.
Build reliability tooling in Python and SQL on BigQuery, and keep monitors and probes defined as code rather than configured by hand.
Retire manual checks by automating them. Operational toil should shrink quarter over quarter, not accumulate.

Why Prolaio?

Impactful Work:
You will join in the fight against heart failure (HF) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with the goal of extending and saving the lives of our patients while also being at the forefront of changing the healthcare industry through technology.
Innovative Environment:
You will be part of an organization doing something that’s never been done before.
Professional Growth:
You will join a growing team and have a substantial impact on our daily and future operations with the opportunity to continuously learn and grow.
Collaborative Team:
You will be part of a team of collaborative, curious, and committed individuals focused on the collective good, inclusiveness, scientific excellence, and advancing digital health for cardiology.

Who You Are?

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
2–5 years in reliability engineering, production operations, hardware or systems test, field failure analysis, or data engineering — in a role where you were accountable for something that had to keep working.
Working SQL and Python: able to pull a dataset, characterize it, and defend the query behind a number.
Experience with a cloud data platform (Google Cloud and BigQuery preferred; AWS or Azure equivalents are fine).
Ability to write up a technical investigation clearly — what was observed, what was ruled out and how, and what remains unknown.

Additional Qualifications (Nice to Haves)

Hands-on exposure to Bluetooth Low Energy (GATT services and characteristics, connection intervals, pairing and bonding, disconnect behaviour), Wi-Fi or cellular data standards — and how each one fails in the field rather than how it is specified to behave.
Battery and power behaviour: discharge characterisation, charge-state interpretation, and telling a measurement artefact from a real capacity defect.
Formal reliability method — FMEA and risk priority numbers, FRACAS practice, and standards such as IEC 60812 or ISO 13485.
Observability tooling (Datadog, Grafana or similar) and synthetic monitoring.
Android device telemetry, mobile application diagnostics, or embedded firmware experience.
Prior work in medtech, digital health, clinical trials or another regulated, patient-facing environment.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

: Competitive salary, performance bonus, and equity so you can share in what we build.
Great Health Coverage:
Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple options and strong company contributions.
Flexible Spending Perks:

Generous paid time off, sick leave, and company holidays.

Plan for the Future

The Role
You'll build, modernize, and operate the platform-wide logging, metrics, and alerting infrastructure that gives Everlaw engineers real-time visibility into how our platform behaves in production. Working across the entire telemetry stack—from core libraries in Java and Python to ingestion pipelines, dashboards, and alerting—you'll ensure our engineering teams can detect, diagnose, and resolve issues while maintaining strict FedRAMP compliance and high availability.
This is a full-time, exempt position based in our Oakland, CA office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.

What you'll do
Build and maintain log, metric, and alert infrastructure across commercial and federal environments using tools such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, and PagerDuty.
Write reusable libraries and integrations in Java and Python that make it easy for engineers to emit structured logs, metrics, and traces from their services.
Develop and manage infrastructure as code with Terraform to ensure dashboards, alert rules, and telemetry pipelines are versioned, reviewable, and reproducible.
Improve our observability architecture by designing telemetry solutions that scale and incorporates emerging AI tools as Everlaw continues to grow.
Improve alert quality and incident response by tuning noisy alerts, creating actionable runbooks, and helping engineers find the necessary signal during live incidents.
Support regulatory and compliance efforts by keeping observability systems thoroughly documented and aligned with FedRAMP and data-handling requirements.
Participate in on-call rotations, respond to production issues, and drive post-incident improvements to prevent recurrence.

About You
You have at least 2 years of professional software engineering experience building, testing, and operating production systems in a cloud environment (AWS preferred).
You are proficient in a coding language such as Java, Go or Python and are comfortable picking up new tools quickly.
You have hands-on experience with observability tools for logging, metrics, or alerting (e.g., Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, InfluxDB, Splunk, PagerDuty, etc).
You have experience with infrastructure as code and container technologies, such as Terraform, Docker, Ansible, or Helm.
You communicate technical concepts clearly and navigate ambiguity by breaking large projects into clear milestones.
You are authorized to work in the United States. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring U.S. employment visas for this role.

Bonus points
Experience with OpenTelemetry or distributed tracing systems.
Experience building or operating telemetry pipelines and log routing at scale.
Experience operating distributed systems or working in regulated environments (FedRAMP, HIPAA, or SOC 2).
Experience reducing alert fatigue and refining incident management practices.

Think you're missing some of the skills and are hesitant to apply? We do not believe in the 'perfect' candidate and encourage you to apply if you feel you can bring value to our team. We often revisit candidates who may have applied for a different role if something comes up that's a better fit.
The Team — Observability
The Observability team builds and evolves the infrastructure, observability, automation, and delivery systems that power Everlaw's engineering organization. By improving cloud architecture, development workflows, and platform reliability, the team helps engineers ship confidently while keeping Everlaw resilient, efficient, and secure. This work reduces friction for developers and ensures the platform performs when legal teams need it most.
Total Rewards & Benefits
The expected salary range for this role is $150,000 to $190,000. Final salary depends on factors including the candidate's experience and skills, and the base pay range is subject to change. This role is also eligible for equity and the benefits below.

Company-sponsored life and disability insurance

Financial rewards

17 paid vacation days, 11 federal holidays, and paid sick leave
Four "Everlawlidays" (additional paid company-wide days off) per year
Annual allocation for learning & development and relevant professional membership dues
Hybrid work with regular work-from-home days and flexibility for life's logistics
Monthly home internet reimbursement, plus a stipend for your desk setup
Catered lunch each workday, plus snacks and company-wide events in our offices

About Everlaw
When a lawsuit or investigation happens, teams must comb through vast amounts of electronic evidence — emails, documents, chats, files — to find what matters. That work is not a side task but the case itself, and where most of the time and money in litigation goes. Everlaw is the litigation and investigation management platform changing that, using AI to turn mountains of messy data into the handful of facts that win or lose a case, compressing weeks of work into hours.
We're the kind of place that's ranked #1 on G2 in our category and named a Great Place to Work™ by our own team. Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

About The Team

HIFI's engineering team builds the payments infrastructure that fintechs and financial institutions use to move money on stablecoin rails. The team owns the APIs, ledger, and on-chain systems behind every payment HIFI processes, and works closely with product and compliance to make sure that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and ready for regulated use. As HIFI's volume grows and more institutions build on our platform, this team will decide how stablecoin payments hold up at the scale and standard that traditional financial infrastructure is held to.

As a Blockchain Engineer
at HIFI you will help own on-chain systems day to day. You'll build and maintain the integrations, smart contracts, and wallet infrastructure that connect HIFI's payments products to the chains and stablecoins we support. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll design how funds move and settle on-chain, work with the rest of engineering to connect those flows to our ledger and APIs, and partner with compliance on controls like wallet screening and transaction monitoring. You'll also be the person the team relies on to judge when a new chain or protocol is ready for production use.

What You Will Build

Wallet infrastructure, including key management, transaction signing, and orchestration across custodial and programmatic wallets.
Onchain transaction handling across EVM chains and the other networks we support, including gas, nonce management, and retries.
Stablecoin minting, burning, and settlement logic that connects USDC and other stablecoins to fiat rails for our on-ramp and off-ramp products.
Integrations with centralized and decentralized exchanges for swaps and liquidity routing, and cross-chain bridging between networks.
A double-entry ledger that keeps onchain balances, banking partners, and customer accounts in sync, with automated reconciliation.
Event listeners, confirmation tracking, and webhooks that give our platform and customers real-time visibility into onchain activity.
Idempotent transaction pipelines with failure recovery and screening hooks, so money moves correctly even when something goes wrong.

You might be a fit if

3+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 1 to 2 years building blockchain systems in production.
Deep familiarity with EVM chains, including transaction lifecycles, gas mechanics, common failure modes, and enough Solidity to read and integrate contracts.
Experience with wallet architecture, such as custody models, signing services, or MPC and HSM-backed setups.
Strong backend fundamentals, including API design, data modeling, and handling consistency and concurrency in distributed systems.
You build financial systems with reconciliation and audit trails by default.
You communicate clearly in code review and in writing.

Nice to have

Experience with stablecoin infrastructure such as Circle, or with connecting onchain and fiat settlement.
Hands-on work with CEX APIs, DEX protocols like Uniswap, or bridge integrations.
Experience building ledgers or double-entry accounting systems.
Exposure to compliance engineering, such as transaction monitoring, address screening, or Travel Rule tooling.
Experience with non-EVM chains like Solana or Tron.
Familiarity with traditional money movement, including ACH, wires, and how funds settle between banks and processors.
Early-stage startup experience building and running a system from scratch.

Why This Role Matters

Every payment HIFI processes eventually settles on-chain, and the institutions behind those payments expect them to work as reliably as a wire or an ACH transfer. This is a chance to build the on-chain systems that hold stablecoin payments to that standard, and to shape how regulated money moves on public blockchains while that infrastructure is still being defined.

Additional Requirement

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About UsWe started as a vertical SaaS company in insurance. We grew into operating our own wholesale brokerage and a programs group. Through that, we've lived the operational reality of applying AI in insurance — what works in production, what breaks, what compounds. We've just closed fresh funding to scale this operating model to retail insurance agencies across the country.
Our CEO, Joey Bouchard, built and ran applied AI teams at Palantir. We bring that technical rigor together with years of hands-on insurance operations experience to help agencies deploy AI that works in the real world. (Why insurance is worth this attention.)
Why this role existsBrokerage execution runs on heroics. Service quality depends on who owns the account, how overloaded they are, and what they happen to remember at the right moment. A submission gets marketed broadly, or it doesn't. A renewal gets the same rigor as new business, or it doesn't. A missing detail gets chased, or it stalls.
We don't think that's inevitable. Brokerage execution can be made systematic: software, automation, and AI carrying disciplined follow-through alongside human experts, inside clear bounds, in a regulated environment.
The hard part isn't the model call. It's governability — making AI accountable enough to trust with real deal flow. Who is the AI acting for? What is it allowed to do? What happens when it's wrong? In a regulated industry, those aren't side questions. They're the engineering problem.We've been answering them inside our own wholesale brokerage for years. That's where we test whether the model actually produces more reliable, scalable, and consistent service. If it doesn't work for us, it doesn't deserve to be packaged for the market. Now we're packaging it.
The roleSoftware Engineers sit at the point where Third Plane, our platform, meets the messy reality of our agency. You own the outcome at QuoteWell, the internal customer. You also own the signal back to the rest of the company.
A typical month: you're embedded at QuoteWell, working alongside our operators. You're identifying the workflows where heroics break down — submissions, renewals, follow-up, the work that today depends on someone's memory — and you're building governed AI execution into those workflows. You're calibrating where humans stay (judgment, relationships, accountability) and where the system carries the standard (follow-through, coordination, attention).
The hardest and most interesting part: making it trustworthy. How AI decisions get reviewed, attributed, and defended. That work is what determines whether any of this can actually live in production.
Then you bring it all back. Engineering, Product, and Design need to know what generalizes and what doesn't, so the platform compounds across every customer instead of fragmenting into one-offs. You're the conduit.
What you'll doBuild governed AI workflows — integrating with AMS, carrier portals, email, and the systems our agency actually runs onIdentify which parts of the agency's operation can be made system-governed without losing the judgment that has to stay with peopleDesign the review, attribution, and override patterns that let a regulated business trust the systemCarry field signal back to Engineering, Product, and Design so the platform scales rather than splinters
What we're looking for1-5 years shipping production software (Python and/or TypeScript a plus)Strong engineering foundation — CS degree typical, talented dropouts welcomeHands-on experience with modern AI application patterns, or the aptitude and hunger to get there fastSomeone we can trust in front of stakeholders: troubleshoot, scope, and reason out loud, in the roomGenuine appetite to learn an industry deeply. Insurance is a financial supply chain puzzle, and we expect you to want to understand itGenuine hustle. The kind of person who walks into Monday with a working prototype of something they spotted on FridayWillingness to travel
What you getA real production model to build on, not a slide deck. Our wholesale brokerage is the proof point — you're scaling something that already works.Direct mentorship from Joey, who built and ran applied AI at Palantir before this.An industry that matters. Insurance is one of the largest financial markets in the world and one of the least systematized.
What we offer our full-time employeesCompetitive salaries + equity in the companyMedical, Dental, and Vision healthcare benefits + FSA and HSA optionsFlexible vacation policy to recharge and live lifePaid membership to One Medical for employees, spouses / domestic partners, and dependentsCompany-sponsored 401K plan (Roth & Traditional)Paid parental leave, generous family forming benefits and up to $5,000 of reimbursements through CarrotUp to $1,000 in home office reimbursements to build a productive space to work remotelyAn opportunity to work on solutions that are redefining the future of commercial insuranceA culture driven by a focus on impact, a shared growth mindset, empowered individuals, and integrity
These first few roles set the cultural tone for everything that comes after. If you want to understand what this role actually is, what it isn't, and what it likely means for your career — apply and reach out.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer, Kernels/CUDA (C++)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.
SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER, KERNELS/CUDA (C++)
We are building one of the world’s largest AI supercomputers from the ground up. As part of the Compute Infrastructure team, you will own both the raw GPU supercomputer and the platform layer that runs on top of it. You will work across the full stack — from low-level GPU kernel optimizations and Linux kernel internals to massive-scale orchestration and virtualization — to make training and inference at SpaceXSI as fast, reliable, and scalable as possible.
This is a broad, high-impact role that combines hardcore supercompute and compute infrastructure work. Your contributions will directly accelerate Grok’s training speed and overall AI progress.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Design, build, and optimize massive GPU clusters for extreme-scale training and inference workloads
Develop and tune low-level CUDA kernels (GeMM, Attention, etc.), using CUTLASS, Tensor Cores, and Nsight for maximum performance
Profile, debug, and eliminate bottlenecks across GPU memory hierarchy, networking fabric, filesystems, and multi-GPU operation
Collaborate closely with AI research teams to deliver production-grade performance and scalability

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
5+ years of experience with low-level system programming in C/C++

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
Deep low-level systems programming (C/C++/PTX/SASS)
Strong experience with large-scale GPU clusters or distributed compute infrastructure at production scale
Hands-on work with GPU kernel optimization (CUTLASS, custom kernels, Nsight profiling)
Track record of building or running high-performance infrastructure for AI workloads (training or inference platforms)
Ability to reason from first principles and optimize for both memory-bound and compute-bound scenarios

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
$200,000 - $375,000 USD
Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.
SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our  Recruitment Privacy Notice.

new_jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Prolaio believes that continuous learning and collaboration can make a significant difference in how heart care is administered. We are creating smarter ways to address heart disease and heart risks by uniting patients, care teams, and researchers on a secure, technology-enabled platform that drives clinical innovation and offers a path towards better patient outcomes.
This is precision cardiology, and we know it’s within reach.

What Will You Do?

The Overview

The Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) will ensure that Prolaio’s cardiovascular data platform reliably captures, transports, and delivers continuous biosensor data from participants to the clinical researchers and trial sponsors who depend on it. In this role, you will build and operate the monitoring, service level objectives, incident response, and automation needed to keep critical data flows healthy, identify failures before they impact studies, and ensure that device downtime never goes unnoticed simply because a shipment record says a device was delivered.

This role is ideal for a self-starter who thrives at the intersection of software reliability, connected devices, and clinical data. You will investigate incidents across the full participant-to-platform stack, combining service telemetry with device data and participant reports to determine whether an issue originated with the hardware, phone, firmware, mobile application, connectivity, or the platform itself. You will turn those investigations into durable improvements, automating manual checks, strengthening observability, reducing operational toil, and building the reliability practices that keep Prolaio’s clinical data complete and trustworthy at scale.

The Specifics

Build monitoring that treats missing data as a failure rather than a quiet day — freshness, volume and quality checks that verify delivery from outside the system instead of trusting a job's exit code.
Define and maintain SLIs, SLOs and error budgets for customer-facing data services, and report attainment honestly, including when the news is bad.
Join the on-call rotation, run incident response, and write blameless postmortems that produce owned follow-up actions.
Investigate device failures end to end: correlate discharge curves, Bluetooth disconnects and wear detection against the participant's complaint, and establish or exonerate each candidate cause on evidence.
Treat the fleet as a population — failure rates per device-month, clustering by build lot, firmware version or site — rather than as a queue of individual tickets.
Close the loop. When an analysis cannot reach a verdict, name the missing metric or threshold and route it back into the diagnostics pipeline so the next case is answerable from telemetry alone.
Build reliability tooling in Python and SQL on BigQuery, and keep monitors and probes defined as code rather than configured by hand.
Retire manual checks by automating them. Operational toil should shrink quarter over quarter, not accumulate.

Why Prolaio?

Impactful Work:
You will join in the fight against heart failure (HF) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with the goal of extending and saving the lives of our patients while also being at the forefront of changing the healthcare industry through technology.
Innovative Environment:
You will be part of an organization doing something that’s never been done before.
Professional Growth:
You will join a growing team and have a substantial impact on our daily and future operations with the opportunity to continuously learn and grow.
Collaborative Team:
You will be part of a team of collaborative, curious, and committed individuals focused on the collective good, inclusiveness, scientific excellence, and advancing digital health for cardiology.

Who You Are?

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
2–5 years in reliability engineering, production operations, hardware or systems test, field failure analysis, or data engineering — in a role where you were accountable for something that had to keep working.
Working SQL and Python: able to pull a dataset, characterize it, and defend the query behind a number.
Experience with a cloud data platform (Google Cloud and BigQuery preferred; AWS or Azure equivalents are fine).
Ability to write up a technical investigation clearly — what was observed, what was ruled out and how, and what remains unknown.

Additional Qualifications (Nice to Haves)

Hands-on exposure to Bluetooth Low Energy (GATT services and characteristics, connection intervals, pairing and bonding, disconnect behaviour), Wi-Fi or cellular data standards — and how each one fails in the field rather than how it is specified to behave.
Battery and power behaviour: discharge characterisation, charge-state interpretation, and telling a measurement artefact from a real capacity defect.
Formal reliability method — FMEA and risk priority numbers, FRACAS practice, and standards such as IEC 60812 or ISO 13485.
Observability tooling (Datadog, Grafana or similar) and synthetic monitoring.
Android device telemetry, mobile application diagnostics, or embedded firmware experience.
Prior work in medtech, digital health, clinical trials or another regulated, patient-facing environment.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

Flexible Spending Perks:

new_jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Prolaio believes that continuous learning and collaboration can make a significant difference in how heart care is administered. We are creating smarter ways to address heart disease and heart risks by uniting patients, care teams, and researchers on a secure, technology-enabled platform that drives clinical innovation and offers a path towards better patient outcomes.
This is precision cardiology, and we know it’s within reach.

What Will You Do?

The Overview

As a Data Engineer in Test, you will play a critical role in advancing Prolaio’s mission to transform heart care. In this position, you will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to validate and optimize data pipelines, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the data infrastructure that underpins our SaMD products. Your work will be essential in delivering scalable, high-quality data systems that directly support the development of life-changing heart care solutions for patients.

We are looking for a highly driven individual with deep expertise in testing data pipelines, analytical workflows, and large datasets. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with cloud-based Data Lake environments (including services like Google Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Databricks, or Snowflake), and generating synthetic data to support testing where real patient data is limited, restricted, or unavailable. Your contributions will ensure the integrity, performance, and scalability of our data infrastructure, aligning with our commitment to delivering safe, effective, and accessible heart care solutions.

The Specifics

Develop and execute comprehensive test plans, test cases, and automated test suites for data pipelines to ensure data quality, consistency, and system performance.
Test and validate ETL/ELT processes and data workflows across Data Lake environments, confirming the accuracy of data transformations and adherence to business logic.
Validate data ingestion, processing, and storage within scalable cloud data platforms such as BigQuery, ensuring computed data correctly reflects raw time-series biosensor inputs.
Design, build, and maintain synthetic data generation tools and datasets that mimic real-world time-series biosensor data, enabling thorough test coverage where real patient data is limited or restricted.
Collaborate with data engineers and data scientists to define testing requirements and ensure data accuracy throughout the entire data lifecycle.
Conduct performance testing and benchmarking on data systems to evaluate scalability under high data loads and identify performance bottlenecks.
Monitor and report on key performance metrics, identifying potential data anomalies, inconsistencies, or performance issues.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of testing processes, automation frameworks, and tools used across data workflows.

Why Prolaio?

Impactful Work:
You will join in the fight against heart failure (HF) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with the goal of extending and saving the lives of our patients while also being at the forefront of changing the healthcare industry through technology.
Innovative Environment:
You will be part of an organization doing something that’s never been done before.
Professional Growth:
You will join a growing team and have a substantial impact on our daily and future operations with the opportunity to continuously learn and grow.
Collaborative Team:
You will be part of a team of collaborative, curious, and committed individuals focused on the collective good, inclusiveness, scientific excellence, and advancing digital health for cardiology.

Who You Are?

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field.
3+ years of experience in software testing, with a specific focus on data pipelines, Data Lake, and data warehouses.
Strong understanding of data engineering concepts and technologies, including ETL/ELT processes, Data Lake , and cloud-based data warehouses.
Proficiency in SQL and Python for data querying, analysis, and test automation.
Experience working with cloud-based data platforms, particularly Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and BigQuery.
Demonstrated experience generating synthetic data for testing purposes, including designing datasets that realistically represent production data characteristics.
Familiarity with data testing tools and frameworks such as pytest, unittest, or TestNG.
Strong knowledge of time-series data processing, analysis techniques, and best practices.
Excellent problem-solving, analytical, communication, and collaboration skills.

Additional Qualifications (Nice to Haves)

Certifications in data engineering or cloud platforms (e.g., GCP Certified Data Engineer, Databricks Certified Data Engineer).
Experience in a regulated industry (Healthcare, MedTech, or BioTech), with familiarity with data governance and regulatory compliance frameworks.
Prior experience testing systems subject to IEC 62304 or similar SaMD quality standards.

: Competitive salary, performance bonus, and equity so you can share in what we build.

Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple options and strong company contributions.
Flexible Spending Perks:
HSA, FSA, commuter benefits, and a $1,200 annual Lifestyle Spending Account to support wellness, commuting, family needs, and more.

Generous paid time off, sick leave, and company holidays.

files

The Role
You'll build, modernize, and operate the platform-wide logging, metrics, and alerting infrastructure that gives Everlaw engineers real-time visibility into how our platform behaves in production. Working across the entire telemetry stack—from core libraries in Java and Python to ingestion pipelines, dashboards, and alerting—you'll ensure our engineering teams can detect, diagnose, and resolve issues while maintaining strict FedRAMP compliance and high availability.
This is a full-time, exempt position based in our Oakland, CA office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.

What you'll do
Build and maintain log, metric, and alert infrastructure across commercial and federal environments using tools such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, and PagerDuty.
Write reusable libraries and integrations in Java and Python that make it easy for engineers to emit structured logs, metrics, and traces from their services.
Develop and manage infrastructure as code with Terraform to ensure dashboards, alert rules, and telemetry pipelines are versioned, reviewable, and reproducible.
Improve our observability architecture by designing telemetry solutions that scale and incorporates emerging AI tools as Everlaw continues to grow.
Improve alert quality and incident response by tuning noisy alerts, creating actionable runbooks, and helping engineers find the necessary signal during live incidents.
Support regulatory and compliance efforts by keeping observability systems thoroughly documented and aligned with FedRAMP and data-handling requirements.
Participate in on-call rotations, respond to production issues, and drive post-incident improvements to prevent recurrence.

About You
You have at least 2 years of professional software engineering experience building, testing, and operating production systems in a cloud environment (AWS preferred).
You are proficient in a coding language such as Java, Go or Python and are comfortable picking up new tools quickly.
You have hands-on experience with observability tools for logging, metrics, or alerting (e.g., Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, InfluxDB, Splunk, PagerDuty, etc).
You have experience with infrastructure as code and container technologies, such as Terraform, Docker, Ansible, or Helm.
You communicate technical concepts clearly and navigate ambiguity by breaking large projects into clear milestones.
You are authorized to work in the United States. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring U.S. employment visas for this role.

Bonus points
Experience with OpenTelemetry or distributed tracing systems.
Experience building or operating telemetry pipelines and log routing at scale.
Experience operating distributed systems or working in regulated environments (FedRAMP, HIPAA, or SOC 2).
Experience reducing alert fatigue and refining incident management practices.

Think you're missing some of the skills and are hesitant to apply? We do not believe in the 'perfect' candidate and encourage you to apply if you feel you can bring value to our team. We often revisit candidates who may have applied for a different role if something comes up that's a better fit.
The Team — Observability
The Observability team builds and evolves the infrastructure, observability, automation, and delivery systems that power Everlaw's engineering organization. By improving cloud architecture, development workflows, and platform reliability, the team helps engineers ship confidently while keeping Everlaw resilient, efficient, and secure. This work reduces friction for developers and ensures the platform performs when legal teams need it most.
Total Rewards & Benefits
The expected salary range for this role is $150,000 to $190,000. Final salary depends on factors including the candidate's experience and skills, and the base pay range is subject to change. This role is also eligible for equity and the benefits below.
Health & well-being

Company-sponsored life and disability insurance

Growth & everyday perks
17 paid vacation days, 11 federal holidays, and paid sick leave
Four "Everlawlidays" (additional paid company-wide days off) per year

Hybrid work with regular work-from-home days and flexibility for life's logistics
Monthly home internet reimbursement, plus a stipend for your desk setup
Catered lunch each workday, plus snacks and company-wide events in our offices

When a lawsuit or investigation happens, teams must comb through vast amounts of electronic evidence — emails, documents, chats, files — to find what matters. That work is not a side task but the case itself, and where most of the time and money in litigation goes. Everlaw is the litigation and investigation management platform changing that, using AI to turn mountains of messy data into the handful of facts that win or lose a case, compressing weeks of work into hours.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, Blockchain
new_jobs.description:
About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

About The Team

HIFI's engineering team builds the payments infrastructure that fintechs and financial institutions use to move money on stablecoin rails. The team owns the APIs, ledger, and on-chain systems behind every payment HIFI processes, and works closely with product and compliance to make sure that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and ready for regulated use. As HIFI's volume grows and more institutions build on our platform, this team will decide how stablecoin payments hold up at the scale and standard that traditional financial infrastructure is held to.

As a Blockchain Engineer
at HIFI you will help own on-chain systems day to day. You'll build and maintain the integrations, smart contracts, and wallet infrastructure that connect HIFI's payments products to the chains and stablecoins we support. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll design how funds move and settle on-chain, work with the rest of engineering to connect those flows to our ledger and APIs, and partner with compliance on controls like wallet screening and transaction monitoring. You'll also be the person the team relies on to judge when a new chain or protocol is ready for production use.

What You Will Build

Wallet infrastructure, including key management, transaction signing, and orchestration across custodial and programmatic wallets.
Onchain transaction handling across EVM chains and the other networks we support, including gas, nonce management, and retries.
Stablecoin minting, burning, and settlement logic that connects USDC and other stablecoins to fiat rails for our on-ramp and off-ramp products.
Integrations with centralized and decentralized exchanges for swaps and liquidity routing, and cross-chain bridging between networks.
A double-entry ledger that keeps onchain balances, banking partners, and customer accounts in sync, with automated reconciliation.
Event listeners, confirmation tracking, and webhooks that give our platform and customers real-time visibility into onchain activity.
Idempotent transaction pipelines with failure recovery and screening hooks, so money moves correctly even when something goes wrong.

You might be a fit if

3+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 1 to 2 years building blockchain systems in production.
Deep familiarity with EVM chains, including transaction lifecycles, gas mechanics, common failure modes, and enough Solidity to read and integrate contracts.
Experience with wallet architecture, such as custody models, signing services, or MPC and HSM-backed setups.
Strong backend fundamentals, including API design, data modeling, and handling consistency and concurrency in distributed systems.
You build financial systems with reconciliation and audit trails by default.
You communicate clearly in code review and in writing.

Nice to have

Experience with stablecoin infrastructure such as Circle, or with connecting onchain and fiat settlement.
Hands-on work with CEX APIs, DEX protocols like Uniswap, or bridge integrations.
Experience building ledgers or double-entry accounting systems.
Exposure to compliance engineering, such as transaction monitoring, address screening, or Travel Rule tooling.
Experience with non-EVM chains like Solana or Tron.
Familiarity with traditional money movement, including ACH, wires, and how funds settle between banks and processors.
Early-stage startup experience building and running a system from scratch.

Why This Role Matters

Every payment HIFI processes eventually settles on-chain, and the institutions behind those payments expect them to work as reliably as a wire or an ACH transfer. This is a chance to build the on-chain systems that hold stablecoin payments to that standard, and to shape how regulated money moves on public blockchains while that infrastructure is still being defined.

Additional Requirement

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. We also provide reasonable accommodations during the hiring process.

new_jobs.description:
About UsWe started as a vertical SaaS company in insurance. We grew into operating our own wholesale brokerage and a programs group. Through that, we've lived the operational reality of applying AI in insurance — what works in production, what breaks, what compounds. We've just closed fresh funding to scale this operating model to retail insurance agencies across the country.
Our CEO, Joey Bouchard, built and ran applied AI teams at Palantir. We bring that technical rigor together with years of hands-on insurance operations experience to help agencies deploy AI that works in the real world. (Why insurance is worth this attention.)
Why this role existsBrokerage execution runs on heroics. Service quality depends on who owns the account, how overloaded they are, and what they happen to remember at the right moment. A submission gets marketed broadly, or it doesn't. A renewal gets the same rigor as new business, or it doesn't. A missing detail gets chased, or it stalls.
We don't think that's inevitable. Brokerage execution can be made systematic: software, automation, and AI carrying disciplined follow-through alongside human experts, inside clear bounds, in a regulated environment.
The hard part isn't the model call. It's governability — making AI accountable enough to trust with real deal flow. Who is the AI acting for? What is it allowed to do? What happens when it's wrong? In a regulated industry, those aren't side questions. They're the engineering problem.We've been answering them inside our own wholesale brokerage for years. That's where we test whether the model actually produces more reliable, scalable, and consistent service. If it doesn't work for us, it doesn't deserve to be packaged for the market. Now we're packaging it.
The roleSoftware Engineers sit at the point where Third Plane, our platform, meets the messy reality of our agency. You own the outcome at QuoteWell, the internal customer. You also own the signal back to the rest of the company.
A typical month: you're embedded at QuoteWell, working alongside our operators. You're identifying the workflows where heroics break down — submissions, renewals, follow-up, the work that today depends on someone's memory — and you're building governed AI execution into those workflows. You're calibrating where humans stay (judgment, relationships, accountability) and where the system carries the standard (follow-through, coordination, attention).
The hardest and most interesting part: making it trustworthy. How AI decisions get reviewed, attributed, and defended. That work is what determines whether any of this can actually live in production.
Then you bring it all back. Engineering, Product, and Design need to know what generalizes and what doesn't, so the platform compounds across every customer instead of fragmenting into one-offs. You're the conduit.
What you'll doBuild governed AI workflows — integrating with AMS, carrier portals, email, and the systems our agency actually runs onIdentify which parts of the agency's operation can be made system-governed without losing the judgment that has to stay with peopleDesign the review, attribution, and override patterns that let a regulated business trust the systemCarry field signal back to Engineering, Product, and Design so the platform scales rather than splinters
What we're looking for1-5 years shipping production software (Python and/or TypeScript a plus)Strong engineering foundation — CS degree typical, talented dropouts welcomeHands-on experience with modern AI application patterns, or the aptitude and hunger to get there fastSomeone we can trust in front of stakeholders: troubleshoot, scope, and reason out loud, in the roomGenuine appetite to learn an industry deeply. Insurance is a financial supply chain puzzle, and we expect you to want to understand itGenuine hustle. The kind of person who walks into Monday with a working prototype of something they spotted on FridayWillingness to travel
What you getA real production model to build on, not a slide deck. Our wholesale brokerage is the proof point — you're scaling something that already works.Direct mentorship from Joey, who built and ran applied AI at Palantir before this.An industry that matters. Insurance is one of the largest financial markets in the world and one of the least systematized.
